pages.title: Frederick C. Robie House
pages.tagline: A study of the 1963 measured survey, Chicago

pages.title: Every line runs with the street
pages.text: A long, low house on a corner lot in Chicago's Hyde Park: two slipped rectangular volumes under broad hipped roofs, with the living and dining rooms raised to the second floor and opened to the street through a continuous band of art-glass doors. The roofs cantilever far beyond the walls and the brick is laid with raked horizontal joints.

pages.title: The raised second floor
pages.caption: Interior. The second-floor living and dining space, one continuous room.

pages.title: One room, divided only by fireplace and stair
pages.text:
The ground floor holds the billiard room and playroom; the second floor is one continuous living and dining space divided only by the central fireplace and stair; the third floor holds the bedrooms.
